title: IBM and AMD Open-Source Pelagos GPU Decoder Framework for Large-Scale qLDPC Error Correction Simulations - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IBM Research and AMD open-sourced Pelagos, a vendor-neutral Triton-based GPU decoder framework for simulating qLDPC error-correction codes at supercomputing scale, reporting up to 97x single-GPU speedups and near-linear 8-GPU scaling on AMD Instinct MI300X/MI355X at ORNL's Lux. A six-company survey (AMD, HPE, IBM, IQM, Riverlane, Xanadu) mapped hierarchical real-time decoding architectures across hardware.

insights.claim: IBM Research and AMD open-sourced Pelagos (pelagos-decoder on PyPI), a vendor-neutral GPU-accelerated quantum error-correction decoding framework for evaluating qLDPC codes at supercomputing scale, announced at SC26.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: AMD is inserting itself into the quantum error-correction compute stack, challenging NVIDIA's CUDA-Q dominance.
insights.locator: IBM Research and AMD have open-sourced Pelagos

insights.claim: Pelagos is written in the open-source Triton GPU language under Apache 2.0, implementing Relay-BP-S in fused kernels that target AMD ROCm/HIP, NVIDIA CUDA and Intel SPIR-V GPUs, with up to 97x single-GPU speedup versus one CPU core.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware-neutral Triton kernels reduce CUDA lock-in for QEC simulation — a modest positive for AMD and Intel GPU relevance.

insights.claim: Pelagos keeps belief-propagation message arrays, convergence flags and candidate selection resident in GPU high-bandwidth memory while autotuning between syndrome-major and edge-major layouts.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: QEC decoding is HBM-bound work — another incremental demand vector for high-bandwidth-memory GPUs.
insights.locator: Written in the open-source Triton GPU programming language

insights.claim: Evaluating fault-tolerant qLDPC codes such as bivariate-bicycle memories requires simulating billions of circuit-level error syndromes to resolve logical error rates down to 10−12.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Fault-tolerance R&D is a structural HPC/GPU workload, tying quantum roadmaps to classical compute spend.
insights.quote: requires simulating billions of circuit-level error syndromes to resolve logical error rates down to 10−12

insights.claim: Pelagos reached 3,845 decodes/s on the One-Gross [[144,12,12]] code using 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (6.23x end-to-end scaling) and 2,686 decodes/s on 8x MI300X.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Concrete AMD Instinct performance numbers for QEC give AMD a benchmarkable foothold in quantum-HPC.

insights.claim: On the Two-Gross [[288,12,18]] code, Pelagos achieved 7.58x GPU decode scaling on eight MI300X GPUs and 7.45x scaling (1,265 decodes/s) on ORNL's Lux MI355X supercomputer.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Near-linear multi-GPU scaling means QEC simulation capacity grows with GPU node purchases.

insights.claim: Replacing single-process threaded dispatch with persistent per-GPU worker processes and shared-memory output buffers cut eight-GPU host preprocessing overhead on two-gross circuits from 3.21 seconds to 0.73 seconds on ORNL's Lux.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Host-side orchestration, not GPU kernels, was a key bottleneck — system software matters for quantum-HPC scaling.

insights.claim: AMD, HPE, IBM, IQM, Riverlane and Xanadu co-authored a hierarchical decoding survey mapping predecoding cascades, sliding-window streaming pipelines and concatenated-code interfaces across CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, ASICs and cryogenic hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cross-vendor collaboration suggests decoding stacks will be heterogeneous — opportunities for FPGA/ASIC suppliers and Riverlane.
insights.locator: Alongside the software release, authors from AMD

insights.claim: Real-time QEC decoding reaction targets span three orders of magnitude, from microsecond superconducting cycles to millisecond-scale trapped-ion and neutral-atom schedules.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Modality determines decoder hardware: superconducting needs FPGA/ASIC-class latency while ions/atoms can use GPUs.
insights.locator: Alongside the software release, authors from AMD

insights.claim: The Pelagos release advances a joint QEC co-design platform established earlier in November 2026 by IBM, AMD and Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM is diversifying classical partners beyond NVIDIA, giving AMD a strategic quantum foothold.
insights.locator: IBM Research and AMD have open-sourced Pelagos
